about: Describe-the-track eval: run with `npm run plan-eval` (scripts/plan-eval.ts). Each case starts from Setup's standard project in `setup` (overridable per case) and runs the same assist loop as Build's Describe track (fresh start, up to 3 repair rounds). Checks are measured on the built project (src/plan/eval.ts): numbers are minimums, booleans must hold. The user's train is the 60052 Cargo Train; until its cars are entered in Setup the example train (3 cars, 672 mm) stands in for it.

cases.description: A simple oval for my LEGO City Cargo Train (60052), using just the track that came with the set.
A bigger oval that uses most of the free floor in front of the KALLAX. Print whatever extra straights it needs.
A figure eight that crosses itself on a 90° level crossing.
An oval with a passing loop on the long side so two trains can pass each other.
An oval with two sidings off the inside of the loop, each ending at a buffer stop, for parking wagons.
An oval with a small freight yard beside it: a ladder of three parallel sidings, each ending on a buffer stop.
A line from one side of the room that ends in a balloon (reversing) loop, so the train turns round and comes back.
An oval in front of the KALLAX, with a branch that runs into a bottom-row cubby from the back, like a tunnel portal through the shelf.
An oval in front of the KALLAX with a siding that runs into a bottom cubby as a little station, ending on a buffer.
A branch that climbs from the oval up to the second shelf row of the KALLAX and ends on a buffer inside that cubby.
A two-turn helix that lifts a branch off the oval to an upper level about 240 mm up, ending on a buffer up there.
Two loops where one goes over the other on a bridge — a flyover, not a level crossing.
A dogbone: a long folded loop with two parallel tracks through the middle and a turning loop at each end.
A big loop that runs right round the edge of the room, passing in front of the KALLAX.
An out-and-back line: it starts at a buffer stop on the left, runs across the room and turns back on a reversing loop at the far end.
An oval with one siding, everything printed in the fast-print style — don't use my LEGO track.
Use only the track I own, nothing printed, but make it more interesting than a plain oval.
I bought one LEGO left and one LEGO right switch. Use them to add a passing loop to my oval.
A figure eight with a passing loop and three sidings.
An oval with R12 curves so the whole loop fits in 300 mm.
